newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares close down on Lujiazui.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares close down on Lujiazui.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index closed down in dull trading on Thursday due to profit-taking in the property developer Luijiazui, but sentiment remained good on expectations of strong growth in China's economy, brokers said.
The index fell 1.283 points or 1.91 percent to 65.743 points, on volume of 11.5 million shares worth $5.3 million.
Brokers said some profit-taking in Lujiazui pushed the index down in the midst of dull trading with holiday sentiment dominating the first session of 1997.
Lujiazui traded the most, falling $0.038 or 3.90 percent to $0.936, on volume of 1.8 million shares.
All 42 B shares traded, with 35 down, two flat and five up.
"Most investors are not yet back from their holiday, which made the trading sluggish," one broker said. "But market sentiment was stable with market fundamentals improving."
"Technical charts indicate the index is unlikely to move up or down sharply in the short term assuming no fresh stimulus," a second broker said.
"Lujiazui's performance will continue to have a big impact on the movement of the index," he added.
Construction machinery maker Jintai was the biggest loser on expectations of poor results, slipping $0.018 or 8.25 percent to $0.200, on volume of 112,000 shares.
Shanghai domestic A shares consolidated up on support buying ahead of the close, but a wait-and-see mood dominated the market in the aftermath of the New Year Day holiday, brokers said.

The A index inched up 3.207 points or 0.34 percent to 958.190 points, on volume of 241.2 million shares worth 2.3 billion yuan. The SSE 30 blue-chip index gained 7.043 points or 0.29 percent to 2449.470 points.
Southeast Medic was the star on speculative demand, soaring limit-up 0.74 yuan to 8.12 yuan, on volume of 1.8 million shares.
